decisive_items: His mother had systemic lupus erythematosus treated with hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisolone and was positive for anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La antibodies
antibody testing confirmed high-titer antinuclear antibodies (>1:1000) and 52-kD anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La positivity
A permanent pacemaker was placed on day 50
response.rationale: Maternal SLE with anti-Ro/La and infant antibody positivity strongly indicate neonatal lupus, which explains both the cardiac conduction abnormality (pacemaker) and progressive pulmonary disease. Congenital heart block is a component but not the full syndrome.

rejected.why: CT ground-glass opacities are nonspecific and BPD lacks typical prematurity/ventilation history; progressive disease despite antibiotics favors immune etiology.
Initial positive cultures responded to antibiotics, but subsequent negative cultures with worsening CT and normal inflammatory markers argue against ongoing pneumonia.
Heart block is a manifestation of neonatal lupus, not an independent diagnosis; antibody profile and maternal history are more specific.
